title: Elko, Nevada — cultural baseline
summary: Elko is a small northeastern Nevada regional center with a demonstrably mining-centered labor market and a conspicuous Western, Basque, and outdoor civic identity. It is not evidence-based to reduce the city to a hunting stereotype or to claim a venture-capital social scene is absent; the available sources establish neither claim directly.

structured.scope: Elko city unless a claim explicitly says Elko County or region.
established: Elko County's current workforce profile and state workforce material support treating mining and mining-adjacent skilled work as a major regional economic anchor.

Elko has enduring, organized Western arts and heritage infrastructure rather than only a generic small-town arts claim: the Western Folklife Center and its National Cowboy Poetry Gathering operate in downtown Elko.
Outdoor and hunting culture is publicly visible in the city through a recurring NDOW-supported Sportsman's Expo with wildlife education, outdoor vendors, and youth activities.

Census data describes a city of about 21,000 people, with 82.8 percent of residents age one or older living in the same house one year earlier. This is a residential-stability signal, not proof that every newcomer will find a close-knit community.
not_established: No source in this baseline establishes that Elko is generally asleep after 8 p.m.; event calendars and a historic saloon are not a representative nightlife census.
No source establishes that children skip school on the first day of turkey season. The local presence of hunting education and an outdoor expo does not support that inference.

No source establishes a citywide rule that people without trade skills are unhireable. Mining is an important anchor, but county data also records retail, health care, government, transportation, and other work.
No source establishes either the presence or absence of a meaningful venture-capital social scene. Absence of evidence is retained as a research gap rather than scored as a negative fact.
structured.comparison_contract: Use the established claims as evidence-backed cultural and economic signals. Treat the not-established claims as unknown. A future city-comparison result must show the distinction.
